intent: Tests never pass the CI job step files (GITHUB_OUTPUT and the rest) to anything they start; isolation.test.js checks the real ones

obligations.text: Existing tests or test setup changed (test/ci-handoff.test.js, test/helpers.js): the old tests still pass on the new code, and a person reviews the change (fast mode: without planted bugs POCP can't show the tests still catch what they caught)

guard.summary: the old tests fail on the new code, and on the base the same checks didn't finish normally ("node --test test/*.test.js" exit 1, timed out), so it can't be told whether they were already failing: a person must approve it

failed_tests: a check that timed out runs again on the next pocp fix

changed_tests.reason: test/runner-step-files.test.js is a test file that was added

failed_tests: eval --corpus marks a check that times out as timeout, not a catch

guard.summary: the old tests already fail at the base ("node --test test/*.test.js" exit 1), so the guard can't tell whether this change altered behavior: a person must approve it. The same tests fail on both sides (the commit hands the check to CI: not run, not proven, said plainly; verify --rerun runs it; a check handed to CI that fails there blocks the merge; --ci-results can never stand in for a check handed to CI; a pull request that turns hand-offs on for itself is judged by the base: it runs its checks, and CI flags any hand-off; a pull request that marks its own check "defer" is judged by the base rules; local mode never hands off: the setting is refused, and a hand-off made elsewhere is no proof here; block mode hands the test guard to CI too, and CI still judges the test change; a pull request of several commits: every hand-off is run once, at the head, by verify; an approved loosening of the guard mode can't let a handed-off guard pass unchecked; a head that is a merge ("Update branch"): hand-offs still run, and a break still fails)
